To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we derived the Lee plate equations for the vibration analysis of electroded piezoelectric crystals by changing the integration bounds in the derivation procedure to signify the dominance of the crystal plate in the electroded plate, which is a new approach to derive the plate equations for electrode plates.
modified Lee plate equations have been derived for the vibration analysis of electroded piezoelectric plate with consideration of stiffness and mass of electrodes.

modified Lee plate equations for the high frequency vibrations of electroded piezoelectric crystal plates with consideration of the electrode effects and stiffness and density of the electrode material are derived.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of Lee plate equations to improve the accuracy in frequency prediction and consideration of electrode effects.
the development of a set of Lee plate equations for the high frequency vibration of electroded piezoelectric crystals.
the development of the modified Lee plate equations for the high frequency vibration analysis of piezoelectrics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Lee plate equation with consideration of electrode mass and stiffness is a practical tool for the vibration analysis of crystal resonators.
the Lee plate equations have been improved to the extent to make them practical for resonator designs with improved accuracy and for consideration of the electrode effects for the first time.

the present work provides a complete and practical set of Lee plate equations for the vibration analysis of piezoelectrical plates with electrodes, and the equations are applicable to the design of resonators and sensors with electrodes of any shape.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

Lee plate equations are modified by changing the integration limit in the dimension reduction to reflect the dominant role of crystal plate, and by adding the electrode effects to the density and stiffness terms in the equations.

we developed the Lee plate equations with improved accuracy in the vicinity thickness-shear frequency and consideration of electrode effects for the analysis of electroded piezoelectric crystal plates for the design and optimization of crystal resonators.

the Lee plate equations are derived for electroded plates with improved accuracy in the frequency prediction for thickness-shear vibration mode, which is the most commonly used mode of operation for crystal resonators.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the modified Lee plate equations can be used for the vibration analysis of electroded piezoelectric plate resonators.

the electrode effects are significant for electroded piezoelectric crystals and the modified Lee plate equations with the consideration of electrode effects can be used for the accurate design of crystal resonators.
the Lee plate equations are modified to consider the effects of the electrode for electroded plates.
